critic_summary: The single failure mode targeted: the loop-2 method's EDA sampled at TradeTick events where |net_v| >= 2 but never re-sampled at the strategy's order-arrival cadence, so the t=-41 SELL-skip-inversion statistic was computed over a distribution (active-window-clustered ticks) that does not match the distribution at which the backtest's gate actually fires (~1Hz uniform arrivals). The researcher flagged this in Attack 2 but the method gave no mechanism to act on it; the pre-registered falsifier ('trade_count rises >3% but P&L falls') was triggered exactly as the tick-vs-arrival sampling gap predicted (trade_count +12.84%, realized_pnl -48.6%). The proposed (but reverted) method adds a mandatory Step 3b 'gate-alignment EDA' pass that recomputes the Step-3 decisive number on a synthetic order-arrival stream at the strategy's cadence, with a hard survival criterion (sign agreement, magnitude >= 50% of tick-level, |t| >= 5); a candidate that loses its signal under arrival-cadence resampling is killed before the critique step, not after the backtest. If this method works in a future loop, I'd expect the next reasoning trace to (a) report two parallel decisive numbers per candidate (tick-level and arrival-aligned) with their delta, (b) show at least one candidate being killed specifically at Step 3b for sampling-distribution shift, and (c) make trade_count predictions in Step 5 that are derivable from the Step-3b firing rate rather than from tick-event counts.
